dedupe_keys.name: shadebench urban building shade simulation benchmark dataset

description: ShadeBench is a multimodal dataset and benchmark for urban shade cast by buildings, published in 2026 by the Data Analytics and Reasoning Lab at Arizona State University as an extension of their DeepShade project (IJCAI 2025). For 34 cities on six continents it provides about 137,000 files at 1024 by 1024 pixels: pairs of simulated shade maps at different times of day with text prompts, aligned satellite images, masked building layouts matched to the simulation, and 3D building meshes in OBJ format, with train and test splits. Shadows follow solar position modelling. The authors define tasks and baselines for shade generation, shade segmentation and 3D building reconstruction, aimed at heat-resilient planning for pedestrians. Access: free download from Hugging Face (DOI 10.57967/hf/9248, image folder format) with a demo site and code on GitHub. Licence and cost: free; the dataset card states no licence, while the paper is CC BY 4.0, so reuse terms should be confirmed with the authors. Caveats: shade is simulated from building geometry only, trees are not modelled, city selection and tile extents are the authors' choice, and it is a machine learning benchmark, not an authoritative map. It supports heat exposure and climate adaptation studies for walking and cycling routes. It complements the CoolWalks and ShadeWalk routing models and the UMEP platform in the catalogue.
